A seat is one maker's punch filed at the assay office. You engrave a touchmark, send three hollow pieces from your forge each quarter, and the office scans the punch face, keeping its wear profile. Punches rest in a vault, one copy each. A mark already on file is refused, since dies wear unevenly and lookalikes drift apart.
Costs run 180 dollars for the die, 450 for registration, 1.20 an assay, 30 for courier, near 700 before a mark lands. Fifty clones clear 35,000 and each must keep shipping.
Two signatures are told apart by nib wear while the letters match.
